author: blu
body: ParseState is threaded functionally: `advance` returns a fresh state and earlier states are reused for backtracking, so it is not a uniquely owned `mutable` record. Its in-place writes go through the __record-set intrinsic.

author: blu
body: stall-pos and stall are the no-progress guard. They are a heuristic and are allowed to leak across a backtrack for the same reason fuel is: both only ever move one way, and answering that the parser is stuck is not a decision any earlier state relies on.

author: blu
body: deck-ceiling is the top of the PARSE scratch reservation, carried here rather than threaded as a parameter because the walk that spends it is parse-top-level, whose twenty recursion sites would each have to pass it. Zero means unbounded, which is what a caller with no reservation of its own gets; compile-parse sets the real ceiling through parse-document. It is only ever read, so it leaks across a backtrack harmlessly, exactly as fuel and stall do.

author: blu
body: Every arm that can spin consumes fuel, so this is the one place both guards have to live: answering True here bails through the check each of those arms already makes.

author: blu
body: A call at the same token as the last one is a step the parser did not take. Counting those, rather than counting calls, is what makes the bound immune to depth: nesting moves the position and resets the count.
